title: Add utilization-over-time API for rightsizing
description:
Add a bucketed utilization-over-time API for pool rightsizing. The API must make inefficient capacity visible, such as 11 hardware-reference workers producing only about 2 worker-equivalents of actual usage.

Metric definitions:
- busy_worker_seconds = sum of task run intervals, clipped to the requested time window or bucket
- available_worker_seconds = integral over time of workers considered available
- utilization_pct = busy_worker_seconds / available_worker_seconds * 100
- worker_equivalents = busy_worker_seconds / window_seconds, representing average concurrent busy workers

Task runtime collection:
- Capture and persist the Taskcluster run resolved timestamp in addition to run_started.
- Use terminal run intervals to calculate busy time.
- Handle intervals crossing bucket boundaries by clipping them to each bucket.

Availability and capacity decisions:
- Do not maintain configured capacity manually; it is expected to drift.
- Derive availability from Taskcluster worker contact data.
- Initially consider a worker available when its last contact is within 60 minutes and it is not quarantined.
- Make the contact threshold configurable and tune it using observed last-contact ages for known healthy workers.
- Record availability transitions rather than periodic pool snapshots.
- For an offline transition, use last_contact + threshold as effective_at.
- For an online transition, use the new last_contact as effective_at.
- Quarantine and unquarantine changes must produce equivalent availability transitions.
- Transition-based storage must correctly represent a worker that disappears and later returns, while keeping storage proportional to state changes rather than polling frequency.

API expectations:
- Accept a selected time range and bucket size.
- Return pool and bucket timestamps, busy worker-hours, available worker-hours, average busy workers or worker-equivalents, utilization percentage, and data coverage metadata.
- Define utilization against available, non-quarantined workers rather than a manually configured or raw retained-worker count.
- Return null or an explicit unavailable status when the denominator is zero.

Coverage and completeness:
- Report collection_started, coverage_pct, and complete for the requested range.
- Startup incompleteness naturally disappears once the entire requested window is after collection began.
- Collection outages or missed recent-task data can create later coverage gaps, so completeness must be calculated rather than assumed.
- Avoid presenting incomplete values as authoritative rightsizing data.

Relationship to pool-classifier-49f:
- Keep job counts and jobs per active worker as separate throughput metrics. They complement utilization but cannot substitute for duration-weighted busy time.

Acceptance criteria:
- Schema migrations support resolved task times and historical availability transitions.
- Collection updates both Postgres and SQLite storage implementations with tests.
- Unit tests cover task and availability intervals crossing bucket boundaries, online/offline/return transitions, quarantine transitions, zero capacity, incomplete coverage, and configurable contact thresholds.
- API integration tests verify filtering, bucketing, formulas, stable JSON fields, and invalid parameter handling.
- API documentation states the formulas and availability semantics.
close_reason: Completed the utilization-over-time stack: task intervals, Taskcluster-derived availability transitions, coverage tracking, bucketed aggregation, versioned API, integration tests, and documentation.

title: Support listed availability for wake-on-dispatch pools
description:
Problem

All workers under the proj-autophone provisioner are wake-on-dispatch. Unlike normal workers, they do not resume Taskcluster contact after reboot until a task is dispatched. The current recent-contact policy marks them unavailable after WORKER_CONTACT_THRESHOLD_SECONDS, causing idle Android capacity to disappear from the denominator and utilization to be overstated.

Design

Add an explicit availability_mode setting to pool configuration with signal-based values:

- recent_contact: current behavior. A worker is available only while lastDateActive is within the configured contact threshold and the worker is not quarantined.
- listed: a worker returned by a successful complete listWorkers observation is treated as eligible capacity while not quarantined, regardless of lastDateActive. A worker absent from a successful complete listing becomes unavailable at observation time.

Configure every proj-autophone pool as listed. Keep recent_contact as the default for other provisioners. Implement this through configuration rather than hard-coding the provisioner name.

Semantics and limitation

For listed mode, available means eligible listed pool capacity, not confirmed live or healthy capacity. Taskcluster provides no signal that distinguishes a dormant wake-on-dispatch Android worker from a physically dead worker that remains listed. Known-bad devices must be quarantined or supplied by a future external health source; otherwise they remain in the availability denominator and can understate utilization. Task-run intervals remain the source of busy time.

API and history

Return availability_mode in utilization API responses so consumers can interpret the denominator. Define a safe cutover for already collected proj-autophone availability history so contact-derived intervals are not silently reported as listed-mode history. This may use an explicit coverage boundary, history reset procedure, or versioned semantics, but must prevent incompatible history from appearing authoritative.

Documentation and live UI

Update the utilization documentation to define both modes and clearly state the listed-mode limitation. Live pages must identify listed-mode pools and explain that availability is based on Taskcluster listing plus quarantine state, not confirmed device liveness. At minimum, surface this on the dashboard and individual pool detail pages without implying that listed workers are verified online.

Acceptance criteria

1. Pool configuration accepts and validates recent_contact and listed; recent_contact is the default.
2. All proj-autophone pools explicitly use listed.
3. Listed workers remain available despite stale or missing lastDateActive, unless quarantined.
4. Workers missing from a successful complete listWorkers observation transition out of listed availability; failed or partial observations do not create false transitions and remain coverage gaps.
5. Existing recent_contact behavior is unchanged for other pools.
6. Utilization API responses include availability_mode.
7. Pre-cutover Android history cannot be mistaken for listed-mode history.
8. Utilization API docs explain mode semantics and the dormant-versus-dead limitation.
9. Dashboard and pool detail pages disclose listed mode and its limitation.
10. Unit, storage, API, and web-page tests cover both policies, quarantine handling, disappearance, collection failure, metadata, and disclosure text.
close_reason: Implemented recent_contact and listed availability policies, safe history cutover, API metadata, UI and documentation disclosures, isolated integration fixtures, and full regression coverage; 78 tests pass.

title: Add pool utilization cards and live API guide
description:
Goal

Surface duration-weighted utilization on individual pool detail pages with a compact first version that answers common capacity questions without requiring API use. Keep the main dashboard unchanged for now. Charts and arbitrary UI range selection are explicitly out of scope for this first version.

Related work

This is related to pool-classifier-d5m (Redesign and simplify the web UI), but it is not blocked by that broader redesign and should remain independently actionable. Preserve compatibility with the existing visual language so a later redesign can move the component without changing its semantics.

Pool detail UI

Add a Utilization section containing four cards for exact trailing windows:

- 1h: trailing 1 hour
- 24h: trailing 24 hours
- 7d: trailing 7 days
- 30d: trailing 30 days, not a calendar-month interpretation

Each card displays:

- duration-weighted utilization percentage
- busy worker-hours
- available worker-hours
- coverage percentage or collection state

Calculate every percentage as total busy worker-seconds divided by total available worker-seconds for the complete window. Do not average bucket percentages and do not cap values above 100 percent. Values above 100 percent should be presented as a possible data-quality issue rather than silently normalized.

Use neutral visual styling because high utilization is not inherently good or bad. Reuse the pool availability-mode badge and the existing listed-mode limitation disclosure near the section.

Coverage and freshness

Only display a utilization percentage when the entire selected window has complete task-run and worker-availability coverage. Otherwise show an explicit state such as Collecting data with the coverage percentage. A complete window with zero available worker time should show No available capacity. Request failures should produce a per-card error state and must not prevent the rest of the pool page or other cards from rendering.

All four windows must share an end timestamp anchored to the latest common complete task and availability coverage boundary, not browser now. With periodic collection, using browser now would create an uncovered tail and make every card incomplete between polls. Display Data through TIMESTAMP plus a human-readable age so users understand freshness. Define the smallest API or storage extension needed to expose this common coverage-through timestamp; a lightweight summary endpoint is acceptable if it avoids redundant probing or repeated database work.

Loading and performance

Load utilization asynchronously so the existing pool detail page can render without waiting for utilization queries. One failed range must not fail the others. Prefer a single summary request or otherwise avoid unnecessary duplicate scans of the same 30-day task and transition history. Do not add four utilization columns or per-pool utilization queries to the main dashboard in this iteration.

Live API guide

Add a live, linked utilization API guide reachable from the Utilization section. Use a pool-aware route or equivalent context so the page can provide a copyable curl example for the current provisioner and worker type.

The guide must document:

- start, end, and bucket_seconds parameters
- inclusive start and exclusive end semantics
- response fields and units
- duration-weighted formulas
- complete, incomplete, unavailable, and coverage behavior
- recent_contact and listed availability modes
- the listed-mode dormant-versus-physically-dead limitation
- quarantine behavior
- the 90-day range and 2,000-bucket limits
- at least one pool-specific copyable curl example

Keep docs/utilization-api.md authoritative or update it alongside the live page so repository and live documentation do not drift.

Acceptance criteria

1. Every enabled pool detail page has a Utilization section with 1h, 24h, 7d, and 30d cards.
2. Cards use exact trailing windows with one shared latest-complete coverage end and display data freshness.
3. Complete cards show utilization, busy worker-hours, available worker-hours, and 100 percent coverage.
4. Incomplete windows show collection progress and no authoritative utilization percentage.
5. Zero-capacity, request-error, and greater-than-100-percent data-quality states are explicit.
6. Card percentages use aggregate worker-seconds, never averages of percentages.
7. The section loads asynchronously and does not delay or break the existing pool detail content.
8. No utilization queries or columns are added to the main dashboard.
9. Listed-mode pools retain a visible explanation that listed capacity is not confirmed device liveness.
10. A pool-aware live API guide is linked from the section and covers parameters, formulas, limits, coverage, modes, quarantine, limitations, and a copyable example.
11. Repository utilization documentation remains consistent with the live guide.
12. Route, API/storage, calculation, rendering, loading, error-state, coverage, freshness, and disclosure tests cover the feature.

title: Expand public pool classifier API
description:
Design and implement additional versioned read-only API endpoints beyond utilization. Prioritized roadmap:

1. GET /api/v1/pools — pool discovery/config: ID, provisioner, worker type, OS, enabled state, schedule, availability mode.
2. GET /api/v1/pools/{provisioner}/{worker_type}/summary — dashboard health snapshot: worker count, alerting count, task totals, success/error rates, freshness/coverage, and availability mode.
3. GET /api/v1/pools/{provisioner}/{worker_type}/failures — failure categories/counts with a bounded time window and optional category filter.
4. GET /api/v1/pools/{provisioner}/{worker_type}/workers — per-worker activity, consecutive failures, quarantine state, and top category; support filters and pagination.
5. GET /api/v1/patterns — classification-pattern registry: name, severity, tags, description, enabled state.

Also add GET /api/v1 as a small discovery document listing endpoints and API version. Implement pool discovery plus the per-pool summary first; they enable external dashboards and automation without exposing the larger worker-level data surface. Define stable response schemas, filtering/pagination, and documentation.

title: Add observed scheduled-to-start lag metrics
description:
Implement Phase 1 of the queue-lag roadmap without requiring Pulse or a full task universe.

Collect, persist, and expose observed scheduled-to-start lag for terminal task runs already discovered through the per-worker polling path.

Scope:
- Use the Queue run timestamps: runs[].scheduled as the candidate readiness/schedulable timestamp and runs[].started as the start timestamp. Verify the exact Taskcluster semantics of scheduled before presenting it as ready_at; retain raw scheduled in storage/API even if a derived label is used.
- Calculate scheduled-to-start duration only when both timestamps are present and ordered.
- Report bounded-window count plus p50/p95 and share started within an explicit, configurable SLO. Prefer duration distributions/percentiles to an average.
- Surface the metric with the label observed start lag (or observed scheduled-to-start lag), clearly stating it covers only jobs that started and were later observed as terminal.
- Do not report a total queued-task count, drop/expiry rate, or a pool-health verdict: this collector cannot see jobs that never ran, so the metric has survivorship bias.
- Keep task/run IDs, scheduled, started, resolved, state, reasonCreated, and reasonResolved available in the data model where practical, to support a later Pulse-backed full-task ledger.
- Add unit/API/storage tests for timestamps, boundary cases, percentiles/SLO share, and the explanatory copy.

Out of scope: Pulse subscription, capture of all task dispositions, expiry/drop detection, and reconciliation; those are later roadmap phases.
